name: EB (Elbow Cross)
description: Short for 'elbow,' one hand crosses over to the opposite elbow instead of crossing wrist-to-wrist like a normal crossover — a tighter, higher cross that most freestyle combos use as a connector move.
tips: Only one hand travels; the other stays put near your hip as the anchor the crossing hand reaches toward.
Keep the cross high, near your chest, so there's enough rope clearance below for your feet.

name: Mummy Kicks
description: Each jump turns into a straight-leg kick out in front of you, alternating legs — arms held out mummy-style for balance while the rope keeps its normal one-pass rhythm.
tips: Kick low and quick rather than high and slow; a hip-height kick is plenty and keeps the timing with the rope.
Keep your supporting knee soft so you don't bounce too high between kicks.

name: Side Swing Criss-Cross
description: You swing the rope beside your hip without jumping, then on the next beat cross your arms and jump through — a swing-into-cross transition that shows up constantly in freestyle routines as a breather between harder tricks.
tips: Keep the swing small and relaxed; it's a pause, not a trick on its own.
Start the cross from the swing's momentum instead of stopping the rope first — a clean handoff keeps the rhythm unbroken.

name: Toad
description: One arm reaches under the same-side lifted leg while the other hand keeps the rope turning normally — an under-the-leg cross that looks dramatic but only needs a small knee lift.
tips: Lift the leg just enough to slide your hand underneath — chasing height makes the timing harder, not easier.
Practice the arm-under-leg reach standing still, without the rope, until it's a reflex.
